drugs.dose: Weight-band dosing per national TB program; Dexamethasone or Prednisolone per CNS TB protocol
drugs.duration: 2 months intensive HRZE, then HR for 10 months (12 months total for CNS TB); steroids tapered over 6-8 weeks
drugs.why: Same four-drug backbone as pulmonary TB but with a longer continuation phase given the severity of CNS involvement; adjunctive corticosteroids are specifically indicated in TB meningitis (unlike most TB) as they reduce mortality and neurological sequelae.

drugs.coverage: Used when rifampicin resistance or treatment failure is identified - requires specialized TB program management.

framework: Unlike pulmonary TB, do NOT wait for microbiological confirmation before starting empiric ATT in strongly suspected TB meningitis - the consequences of treatment delay (death, severe neurological sequelae) outweigh the stewardship cost of treating a small number of false positives.
Adjunctive corticosteroids are a key, specific intervention for TB meningitis (reducing mortality) and should not be omitted - this differs from most other TB presentations.
Still send CSF for AFB smear, CBNAAT/Xpert, and culture even though treatment should not wait for results - confirmation remains important for resistance testing and case registration.
Monitor closely for hydrocephalus and raised intracranial pressure, which may require neurosurgical intervention (CSF diversion) independent of antitubercular therapy.

references: National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) India Guidelines
